status: source-repaired; native browser acceptance and independent review pending
root_cause: Current Chrome imperative WebMCP contract uses document.modelContext, asynchronous getTools/registerTool, executeTool(RegisteredTool,object), execute callback and AbortSignal lifecycle. Existing handlers and registration instead read navigator.modelContext, used tools/callTool/run fallback, and did not await registration.
confirmed_red: Strict document.modelContext-only source fixture drove current handler and registration functions through chrome.scripting.executeScript and failed all three assertions on the original source under webmcp-native-red-20261007. The fixture is a mocked API boundary, not native browser acceptance.
repair: Handlers use documented API only and keep assigned-tab targeting, admin/tier/schema metadata and canonical router unchanged. Calls discover by name then pass the discovered object and JSON object input to executeTool. Registration awaits each tool with execute callback and AbortSignal; re-registration aborts previous registration for the same name. On any registration failure, newly added registrations in this pass are aborted and count is reported as 0. Existing page-to-service-worker bridge and dispatch permission/consent path are unchanged; comments and category text now match the documented API.
sibling_census: EXT-F-4118 availability, EXT-F-4119 listing, EXT-F-4120 call, EXT-F-4162 canonical router (delegates unchanged), and EXT-F-4014 list_webmcp_tools category discovery metadata. Bridge/bootstrap comments were stale; source references corrected. No other navigator.modelContext code path found outside revised proposal/report history.
limitations: No Chrome 149+ native API observed or executed; Chromium 141 installation provenance is insufficient for native acceptance.

Strict fixture verifies source contract boundary only. It does not prove browser feature enablement, same-origin exposure, agent advertisement, dispatcher Ask/Act behavior or installed extension behavior.
